fact: IMF PortWatch recorded 4 transits on Oct 4 vs. pre-crisis baseline of 85/day; Brent at ~$103-104/bbl; Gulf sulfur shipments collapsed to 147,000 MT in June vs. 11-year floor of 730,000 MT; FAO reports 3-4 Mt/month of fertilizer trade stalled; strait effectively closed since Feb 28 2026 with ongoing vessel attacks and deadlocked negotiations (straits.live, IFPRI, FAO/openknowledge, Oct 12 2026)

dissent.view: Some dark/AIS-off tanker transits are occurring and Gulf crude exports recovered to ~81% of pre-war levels in September via alternative routes (East-West pipeline, Cape diversion), suggesting physical oil supply disruption is less severe than a hard closure implies.

(Sources: straits.live live tracker 12 Oct 2026; IMF PortWatch Oct 4 2026; GulfNews/OilPrice.com Oct 12 2026)

dissent.view: BISI (Oct 2026) reports that the one-year suspension of October 2025 controls has been extended to 10 January 2027 following a Trump-Xi Washington summit, suggesting a modest easing on the extraterritorial track; however, the core April 2025 licensing regime remains unaffected by this extension.

General licenses exist but are limited to three named Chinese producers (JL MAG, Zhongke Sanhuan, Ningbo Yunsheng) covering only pre-vetted named customers. In June 2026 MOFCOM added 10 US entities including MP Materials to its export-control list. Sources: cmgm.net (2026-08), blog.gettransport.com (2026-07), techtimes.com (2026-10-06), bisi.org.uk (2026-10-01).
rationale: The regime meets Rubric Level 1 on three independent grounds: (a) general licences cover only a whitelist of three named producers and their pre-cleared customers, not most export volume; (b) typical processing exceeds 30 days (60–120+ days in practice); and (c) new categories were added within the trailing 3 months (US entity-list additions including rare-earth supply-chain players in June 2026). Level 2 is not warranted because licences are actively being issued and no categorical suspension or country-wide denial is in effect.

fact: Three confirmed major-mine disruptions active simultaneously: (1) Grasberg Block Cave (world #2) running at ~60% of capacity during phased ramp-up following Sep 2025 mud rush, with 2026 output ~35% below pre-incident forecast per Freeport 10-Q filed 2026; (2) Kamoa-Kakula (top-5 globally) 2026 guidance cut from 420,000 t to 290,000-330,000 t after 2025 seismic/flood event plus a 56-day smelter shutdown in Q2 2026 (mining.com, April 1 2026; Ivanhoe Q2 2026 release); (3) Antofagasta Centinela strike by 709 workers since Oct 7 2026, mining/haulage/development disrupted with unions projecting ~50% output cut in November (northernminer.com, discoveryalert.com, Oct 8-12 2026). rationale: Three named top-20 mines (Grasberg, Kamoa-Kakula, Centinela) have confirmed, physically measured production cuts currently active, satisfying the >=3 threshold; additionally, multiple institutions (Goldman Sachs, BMI) have explicitly forecast a market deficit attributable to these combined losses, satisfying both prongs of the rubric's level-2 definition.

dissent.view: Senegal ECF and Guinea ECF staff-level agreements, plus Bangladesh new programme negotiations, could be counted as early-stage distress signals by some analysts, pushing toward RISING if Board approval comes through in Q4 2026

However, 10y yields are at 30-year highs on persistent fiscal concern and the full funding path for Takaichi's stimulus programme remains credibly unspecified per market analysts, satisfying the rubric's UNCLEAR condition of 'funding path unspecified OR yield up >25bps on fiscal news but auctions still clearing.'

dissent.view: Fitch and S&P both show Stable outlooks at their most recent reviews (Aug and May 2026 respectively), suggesting no further deterioration post-cut — one could argue current posture is band 1 if trailing-12M window is read narrowly to exclude the Oct 2025 cuts

Moody's negative outlook also independently satisfies band 1, but the S&P cut is the most severe signal and triggers band 2.

fact: On 22 June 2026, China MOFCOM issued Announcement No. 23 of 2026, adding 10 US entities to its export control list; the two named US rare-earth producers are MP Materials Corp. and USA Rare Earth Inc. The restriction bans Chinese exporters and all global parties from supplying Chinese-origin dual-use items to those specific firms. Source: MOFCOM Announcement No. 23 of 2026, corroborated by Bloomberg (2026-06-22), Al Jazeera (2026-06-22), Benchmark Minerals (2026-06-22), and Morgan Lewis (2026-07-01). rationale: Two named US rare-earth producers (MP Materials, USA Rare Earth) are on China's MOFCOM export-control list as of 22 June 2026, satisfying rubric level 1 (entity-specific). The restriction is firm-specific, not a categorical sector-wide or class ban on all US rare-earth producers, so level 2 is not warranted.

fact: Per Valuation Research (Oct 2, 2026), average redemption requests across 11 of the 14 largest non-traded BDCs stood at 13.0% in Q3 2026, still well above the standard 5% quarterly cap, with named funds including Blackstone BCRED (~$79B, gated at 5% after ~10% requests per Yardeni/Bloomberg Sept 2026), Cliffwater Corporate Lending Fund (~$31B, capped at 5% after 16% requests), and Blue Owl OTIC/funds (capped at 5%, 39% requests) all actively gating in Q3; in Q2 2026 Fitch tracked 10 of 16 BDCs breaching caps on $15.6B in requests (Fitch/angelinvestorsnetwork.com, ~Aug 2026); cumulative gated AUM across BCRED, Apollo ADS, BlackRock HLEND, Ares ASIF, Cliffwater, Partners Group, Blue Owl funds exceeds $250B.
rationale: The rubric threshold for WIDESPREAD is >=3 of the largest funds gating in the same quarter or combined AUM >$100B; at least 7-10 named major funds have simultaneously breached their 5% quarterly repurchase caps across Q1-Q3 2026 with combined AUM well exceeding $250B, satisfying the WIDESPREAD criterion by a large margin. Corroborating signals include: FOMC policy anchored at 3.50-3.75% (higher-for-longer), sticky CPI at 4.2%, new direct-lending issuance down ~40%, and a $14B cumulative redemption backlog reported by Bloomberg (July 2026), all consistent with structural funding stress in semi-liquid private credit vehicles.

fact: FDIC failed-bank list shows 5 US bank failures in the trailing 6 months (Apr 12-Oct 12 2026): Community Bank and Trust-West Georgia (May 1), Kentland Federal S&L (Jul 10), Small Business Bank (Jul 17), Tioga-Franklin Savings Bank (Aug 21), and Nano Banc (Sep 25, $736M assets). Source: fdic.gov/bank-failures/failed-bank-list (Oct 2026); americanbanker.com (Sep 28 2026); fintechcowboys.com/bank-failure-alert-nano-banc.
rationale: Within the trailing 6 months, at least 1 confirmed CRE-linked failure (Nano Banc, $736M assets, <$10bn) with a public enforcement action explicitly citing CRE concentration satisfies the ISOLATED threshold of 1-2 such failures each <$10bn plus >=1 new enforcement action/consent order citing CRE concentration. CLUSTER (2) is not warranted because credible sources do not firmly attribute >=3 in-window failures primarily to CRE exposure, and no single failure exceeded $10bn or triggered a coordinated interagency action.

fact: At least 6 distinct new major-economy trade measures against Chinese exports were enacted in the trailing 3 months: (1) EU definitive anti-dumping on Chinese car/lorry tyres (4.3%-45.3%), published July 7, 2026 (policy.trade.ec.europa.eu); (2) EU definitive anti-dumping on Chinese polyamide filament yarns (60%-67.6%), EU Reg. 2026/1823, July 27, 2026 (catts.eu/august-2026); (3) EU provisional anti-dumping on Chinese benzyl alcohol, July 27, 2026 (catts.eu/august-2026); (4) Canada CBSA provisional anti-dumping/CVD on unarmored building cables from China, effective July 29, 2026 (catts.eu/august-2026); (5) China extended anti-dumping on single-mode optical fiber from India, effective August 14, 2026 (catts.eu/august-2026); (6) US imposed 7.5% overcapacity tariff on China restoring ~20% total rate, reported August 24, 2026 (china-briefing.com). Simultaneously, the US-China bilateral truce was extended two months on September 27, 2026 (rvia.org), and US-China recommended $30bn in mutual tariff cuts (euronews.com, September 28, 2026). EU safeguard tariffs on Chinese hybrid EVs are under active deliberation but not yet enacted (asiatimes.com, October 9, 2026).
rationale: Six or more new measures in the trailing 3 months satisfies the rubric threshold of >=4 new measures for ESCALATING (score 2), and the EU tyre anti-dumping (up to 45.3%) qualifies as a broad tariff round exceeding 10% across a sector. The ongoing US-China truce extension prevents a clean 'truce breakdown' characterization, but the measure count and sectoral breadth independently clear the ESCALATING bar.

fact: India placed the 1960 Indus Waters Treaty (IWT) in 'abeyance' on 23 April 2025 following the Pahalgam terror attack and continues to hold it so as of October 2026. On 31 August 2026, the Permanent Court of Arbitration (The Hague) ruled unanimously that the IWT remains fully in force and India's abeyance is legally impermissible; India rejected the ruling and the court's jurisdiction. Pakistan's Deputy PM raised the abeyance with the UN Secretary-General on 6 October 2026. No deliberate physical flow cut-off or armed clash has been documented. (Sources: pakera.pk, 11 Oct 2026; Al Jazeera, 1 Sep 2026; ISAS NUS, 28 Apr 2026)
rationale: The IWT is formally contested/suspended by one party (India) and rejected as such by the other (Pakistan), with active UN Security Council diplomacy and an international arbitral ruling — squarely a 'treaty suspended/contested with official threats exchanged' scenario. No kinetic action or confirmed physical diversion of water has been reported, so the threshold for level 2 is not met.

This maps unambiguously to rubric level 2 (confirmed curtailment of data-center load and a declared grid emergency).
